items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 8, 2026
items.excerpt: 08 November 2026• Update: 08 November 2026 Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start Sunday, including Poland's interior minister's claim that far-right ideologies may have influenced a Krakow attacker; Israeli President Isaac Herzog's appointment of Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government; and the US army's announcement of a new task force to disrupt Iran's supply routes. Initial indications suggest that the suspect who opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, was influenced by far-right ideologies, according to Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski. Kierwinski told a news conference that police opened fire on the suspect three minutes after receiving the first report of the attack. He confirmed that six people were killed, including one foreign national, while 16 were injured, including five foreign nationals, two police officers and the suspect. - Israel’s President Herzog says he will task Eisenkot with forming next government Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced that he will task Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government, Israeli news site Ynet reported. Eisenkot has been invited to receive the mandate at a ceremony at the President’s Residence on Sunday at 5 pm local time (1500GMT), according to the report. Once he receives the mandate, Eisenkot will have 28 days to form a government. Herzog can grant an extension of up to 14 days under Israel’s Basic Law. - US army announces new task force to disrupt Iran’s supply routes The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the establishment of a new task force aimed at disrupting Iran’s use of land routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials, expanding Washington’s pressure on Tehran. In a statement on US social media platform X, CENTCOM said Adm. Brad Cooper, the command’s chief, directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate on Nov. 7. The unit, comprising approximately 20 civilian and military personnel, will be based in Tampa, Florida. The task force will work with other US government agencies to monitor and prevent the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and what Washington describes as illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea.

items.excerpt: Israel’s president taps opposition candidate Eisenkot to form a government, in setback for Netanyahu JERUSALEM (AP) — Israeli President Isaac Herzog said Saturday night that he was giving opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a governing coalition following elections on Oct. 27. He has up to six weeks to form a coalition, a challenging task in a deeply divided country reeling from the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks and the three years of wars that have followed in Gaza and beyond. In discussions with the president this week, representatives from most of Israel’s main parties recommended Eisenkot be tasked with assembling a new government. But putting together the parliamentary majority needed remains fraught and any possible coalition would require candidates to make tough compromises that could outrage their own voters. WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president. White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House. Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to “the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior” to become the Republican president's chief spokesperson. White, who was in London on Saturday for a boxing event, was asked at a news conference about Trump's post and responded by saying that he planned to fly to Washington right after and meet with Trump on Monday. KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — A Polish man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow on Saturday and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him, authorities said. The attack, which Poland’s defense minister described as an “act of terror,” happened in Main Square, which is in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town and is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city. The 25-year-old attacker drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each stop with an automatic weapon, authorities said. Although they didn’t release his name, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the man holds “very radical” and “ultranationalistic” views. Hours after the attack, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities found the bodies of three of the suspect's close family members — two women and a man — inside of his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.

items.title: US inflation set to cool in October after two months of sharp increases | World News - Business Standard
items.excerpt: ## The consumer price index is seen rising 0.3% after a 0.6% increase that was the largest since April, based on the median projection in a Bloomberg survey of economists ahead of Tuesday's release ... Bloomberg 8 min read Last Updated : Nov 08 2026 | 1:03 PM IST By Vince Golle and Craig Stirling Prices for US goods and services probably rose at a slower pace in October after two particularly uncomfortable months for American consumers. The consumer price index is seen rising 0.3% after a 0.6% increase that was the largest since April, based on the median projection in a Bloomberg survey of economists ahead of Tuesday’s Bureau of Labor Statistics’ release. The core measure, which excludes often-volatile energy and food components, also probably cooled. The survey median sees a 0.2% increase for October, which would be the smallest advance in three months. The agency won’t publish year-over-year figures after it skipped the October 2025 CPI release due to the federal government shutdown at the time. ## The Fed is expected to hold rates steady. Warsh will have to explain why ## Fed Chair Warsh stresses price stability, offers no signals on rate outlook The October CPI will be the last before the Federal Reserve’s meeting in December, at which investors expect policymakers to boost interest rates. Economists will also assess the finer details of the report for clues on inflation risks into early 2027. Economists at Citigroup Inc. said in a recent note that they anticipate limited pass-through of high energy costs to goods prices, as well as moderate services inflation. What Bloomberg Economics Says... > “We expect headline CPI slowed to 0.25% in October (vs. 0.65% prior). The core likely softened to 0.24% (vs. 0.33% prior), with both softer goods and services price gains driving the improvement. For goods, used cars and consumer electronics — categories that have faced pressure from the AI boom — saw slower inflation. For services, gains in owners’ equivalent rent are down a third from a September spike.” > > > > —Anna Wong, Troy Durie and Eliza Winger The latest snapshot of inflation also follows Friday’s stronger-than-expected October jobs report. Sustained employment growth has the potential of ensuring consumers keep spending, while allowing the Fed to keep its focus squarely on inflation. Another price report, due on Friday, is projected to show nagging inflationary pressures faced by companies. The producer price index is forecast to accelerate to 6.6% for the year through October, the steepest annual increase in nearly four years.

items.title: Fed policymakers consider rate hike after strong jobs report - The Korea Herald
items.excerpt: Published : Nov. 8, 2026 - 10:24:06 Hiring signs are ... AP-Yonhap A stronger-than-expected US jobs report bolstered the case for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, which had lost some momentum ‌amid a post-election stock market selloff and growing fears that weaker AI-driven demand could undercut the economy. Employers added 165,000 jobs last month, more than twice what economists had expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday, and the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 percent. Average hourly wages gained 3.1 percent from a year earlier, not enough to keep up with a 3.7 percent rise in consumer prices that is ‌taking a bigger chunk of the typical paycheck's purchasing power. After the US central bank left its policy rate on hold last month, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said policymakers would be watching for "the accumulation of data" to help decide whether more monetary policy tightening would be needed. For San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly, the latest monthly jobs report appeared to put a definitive tick in the "yes" column. "People are just at the point where they're — they say 'Inflation — I'm doing well ⁠in everything, except I can't keep up with inflation,' so that has to be our number one priority, and the fact that we have a solid labor market gives us the latitude, really, to just get that job done," Daly said in an interview on CNBC. "My expectation is, we're going to have to tighten policy further," said Daly, who is not a voting member of the Fed's policy committee this ⁠year but typically voices views similar to the majority view. Noting "how volatile the world seems to be in many ways," she added, "those volatilities are something that you have to take into account, collect more information, and be deliberate but more gradual in how you get there when you don't know exactly where you're going to need to head. But more is likely to be ​needed and certainly we're prepared — I'm prepared — to do that, if that's what the economy calls for." In comments at a St. Louis civic event Friday, St. ‌Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said inflation remained the top concern in his conversations with businesses in his district. "Inflation is a regressive tax, a distortionary tax," said Musalem, who has advocated for further rate ‌increases. "The best thing we can do for growth ‌and employment is bring inflation back down on a timely basis." He did not address a recent swoon in stock markets driven lower by new doubts about ‌the pace and sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom, but said for now he feels the emerging ​industry is feeding higher inflation through demand for commodities such as copper. Even if that pays off in future profit and productivity, "we need to make monetary policy for the economy of the day, not what it may be ⁠five years from now," Musalem said, and on that basis, for now at least, AI investment "will continue to contribute to inflation." ... The jitters over AI also prompted traders to back away from what had been big bets on a ⁠Fed rate hike next month, figuring that a slowdown in AI-related demand could cool economic growth and ease inflationary pressures, ⁠making further monetary policy tightening a ⁠less urgent matter. The ‌release of the latest employment report, however, put a Fed rate hike back in focus. Markets were pricing about an 80 percent chance of a quarter-percentage-point policy rate increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, up from about 67 percent Thursday. Traders now also see the next and final rate increase coming earlier, in April instead of June, as the central bank battles inflation that has been running above its 2 percent target for more than ​five years. "This is a very strong labor market report on the heels of solid GDP and consumer spending data last week, reinforcing the economy's positive momentum," Olu Sonola, an analyst at Fitch Ratings, wrote after the report. Recent concern over AI poses a risk to that outlook, Sonola said, "but for now the economy remains on firm footing. The labor market's resilience keeps the Fed focused on inflation and pushes the policy debate further toward a December rate hike." (Reuters)

items.title: U.S. Companies' Inflation Concerns Reach Highest Level in Over Two Years | Aju Press
items.excerpt: by BAE IN SUN Posted : November 8, 2026, 15:16 Updated : November 8, 2026, 15:16 U.S. companies' concerns about inflation have surged to their highest level in over two years. Rising oil prices, increased raw material costs, and logistics expenses are intensifying cost pressures on businesses, drawing attention to key U.S. inflation indicators set to be released this week. In last month's series of third-quarter earnings reports, inflation was a central topic. According to Bloomberg, companies in the S&P 500 mentioned the term 'inflation' 820 times during their October earnings conference calls, marking the highest monthly count since February 2024. In the first week of November, mentions of inflation by companies have already surpassed the total for November of last year, Bloomberg reported. By sector, industrial companies, which include machinery, equipment, construction, and transportation, had the highest number of inflation mentions at 213. Basic materials companies, including steel, chemicals, and metals, followed with 135 mentions. This reflects companies' concerns about rising production and operational costs due to raw material and energy prices, as well as logistics expenses. The impact of inflation is also spreading to consumer goods companies. U.S. automaker General Motors (GM) projected that rising raw material, logistics, and memory semiconductor prices will lead to approximately $2 billion in additional costs this year. Of this, about $400 million is attributed to inflation, with most of the impact expected in the fourth quarter. As companies face increasing cost burdens, there are concerns that price pressures at the production stage will transfer to consumer prices. If inflationary trends strengthen again, it could influence the Federal Reserve's monetary policy. According to the CME FedWatch on November 6, futures markets reflect a 76.33% probability that the Fed will raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points at its December Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, up from 66.9% the previous day. Inflation pressures are expected to be confirmed in key U.S. inflation indicators to be released this week. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for October will be published on November 10, with expectations of a 0.3% increase from the previous month, a slowdown from September's 0.6% rise. However, due to a government shutdown in October 2025, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) was unable to collect price survey data, so year-over-year comparisons will not be available this time. On November 13, the Producer Price Index (PPI) for October will be released. Bloomberg anticipates that the October PPI will rise by 6.6% compared to the same month last year, exceeding the previous month's increase of 6.3%. If market forecasts hold true, this would represent the highest level in nearly four years. The PPI, also known as wholesale prices, reflects changes in the prices received by companies for producing and selling goods and services. Increases in production stage prices can affect companies' costs and selling prices, ultimately impacting consumer prices, making it a key indicator for gauging inflation trends.

Two top Justice Department officials resign as post-election exodus accelerates Two top officials at the US Department of Justice resigned on Friday, accelerating an exodus of senior figures from the department following the midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump's Republicans lost control of Congress. The departures of John Eisenberg, who headed the DOJ's National Security Division, and Jason Reding Quiñones, who pursued probes into ‌past criminal investigations of Trump, follow the resignation of civil rights unit chief Harmeet Dhillon on Thursday. Mississippi US Senate candidates battle over ballots as winner remains unclear US Senate candidates in Mississippi are battling over the treatment of ballots still being counted in the race, one of two remaining Senate contests yet to be called after Tuesday's midterm elections. The outcome in Mississippi and in Alaska, where the Senate race is also not yet called, will determine whether the Democratic Party extends its sweeping election victory in which it seized at least 54 of the Senate's 100 seats, and also took control of the US House of Representatives. ... US anti-trans ballot wins pose challenge for Democrats ahead of 2028 Voters in four US states approved ballot measures to restrict transgender rights in Tuesday's midterm elections, sending a warning to Democrats on an issue that has divided the party and is likely to remain a political challenge heading into the 2028 presidential race. The measures succeeded even as Democrats swept to victory nationwide and retook control of Congress, suggesting voters who backed Democratic candidates were still receptive to some Republican arguments on transgender issues. Top US House Democrat on trade issues committed to reversing 'unjustified' tariffs US Representative Richard Neal, the Democrat who is expected to regain the chairmanship of the tax- and trade-focused House Ways and Means Committee, said on Friday that he is committed to reversing President Donald Trump's "unjustified" tariffs and "backroom deals" on trade. In an address to a trade conference hosted by the Biden administration's former US Trade Representative, Katherine Tai, Neal said Trump's "deliberately chaotic and unjustified trade policies" had contributed to rising living costs and growing inequality between workers and the wealthiest Americans.

items.title: Adam Driver wont return for Girls reboot | Mint
items.excerpt: PTI Published 8 Nov 2026, 09:48 AM IST Adam Driver wont return for Girls reboot Los Angeles, Nov 8 (PTI) Actor Adam Driver won't return to reprise his role in the reboot of the 2012 series "Girls", which served as a breakthrough for him. The actor starred as Adam Sackler in the original series, which concluded in 2017 after nine seasons. The announcement of the reboot had fans thinking if the actor will step into Sackler's shoes again. When asked about the return to the series, Driver confirmed he isn't in the project. "No, but I wish them the best of luck," he told Cinema Blend in an interview. The series revolved around four twenty-something women navigating the messy, awkward, and often humiliating realities of post-collegiate life in New York City. It featured Lena Dunham as Hannah Horvat, Lena Allison Williams as Michael , Jemima Kirke as Jessa Johansson and Zosia Mamet in the role of Shoshanna Shapiro, among others. "Girls" was created by Lena Dunham, who is returning for the reboot series, which will comprise five episodes. Williams, Kirke, Mamet (Shoshanna), and Andrew Rannells are also set to return for the series.

items.title: Emma Stone Joins 'The Catch' Co-Star Druski During His 'Saturday Night Live' Opening Monologue, Jokes He Misread Scenes In Their Movie - Watch Now! | Just Jared - Celebrity News, Entertainment News & Photos
items.excerpt: AJ Pitts Nov 8, 2026 · 2 min read ... Emma Stone returned to the Saturday Night Live stage this weekend! The 38-year-old actress, who hosted the show five times, joined this week’s host Druski during his opening monologue on Saturday night (November 7). If you didn’t know, they are set to co-star in the upcoming movie, The Catch. “I am living proof you can bet on yourself and make your dreams come true,” Druski said in his monologue. “I just finished filming my first-ever movie with Emma Stone and she is right now.” > Druski’s monologue! https://t.co/RnaI5AkQpb > > — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) November 8, 2026 After she walked on stage, Druski said, “I’m actually playing her love interest in the new movie that we just did.” “I think you might have misread that in those scenes, because we weren’t love interests in the film,” Emma replied. “But now it is starting to make more sense why you kept looking at me like that for all those scenes.” “That’s probably why we ain’t kiss either,” he said, to which she said, “Yeah.” “If there’s a part two, we’ll get it done,” Druski added. ... ### What is The Catch about? Emma and Druski‘s upcoming movie is actually being directed by her husband, Dave McCary. Plot details are currently being kept under wraps, but it is said to be a baseball rom-com in the vein of Bull Durham and Notting Hill, according to Deadline, and Emma plays “the most hated woman in baseball.” They also say Druski will play Emma‘s security guard in the film. Chris Pine also stars, along with Saturday Night Live‘s Ashley Padilla as Emma‘s sister.

items.excerpt: الأحد 08/نوفمبر/2026 - 01:08 ص شهد الوسط الفني خلال الساعات الماضية حالة من النشاط والتفاعل، وذلك بالتزامن مع استعداد عدد من نجوم الغناء لإحياء مجموعة من الحفلات ... ### أنوسة كوتة تحسم الجدل لـ"وشوشة" بشأن استبعاد إليسا أغنية محمد رحيم من ألبومها حسمت أنوسة كوتة أرملة الموسيقار الراحل محمد رحيم، الجدل المثار حول استبعاد الفنانة إليسا إحدى أغنياته من ألبومها الغنائي الجديد، وما تردد بشأن وجود خلافات بينهما، كاشفة حقيقة الأمر وموقفها من قرار إليسا. وتحدثت أنوسة كوتة في تصريح خاص لـ"وشوشة"، قائلة: "مفيش مشاكل، ودي رؤيتها الفنية"، كما وجهت رسالة إلى الفنانة إليسا بمناسبة طرح ألبومها، قائلة: "ألف مبروك على الألبوم". ... ### أحمد السماحي لـ"وشوشة": ألبوم الموسيقى العربية أعاد أحمد سعد إلى منطقة الطرب أثار الفنان أحمد سعد اهتمام الجمهور بألبومه الجديد الموسيقى العربية، الذي يقدم من خلاله تجربة غنائية مختلفة تعتمد على الطرب والأغنية الشرقية، بمشاركة نخبة من الشعراء والملحنين والموزعين، وهو ما دفع الناقد الفني أحمد السماحي للتعليق على التجربة وتقييم خطوات سعد الفنية. وتحدث الناقد الفني أحمد السماحي في تصريح خاص لـ"وشوشة"، عن رأيه في ألبوم الموسيقى العربية، قائلًا:" أرى أن تجربة أحمد سعد في ألبوم الموسيقى العربية تستحق التوقف عندها بقوة، لأن أحمد سعد لم يعد مجرد مطرب يمتلك صوتًا قويًا وقدرة على تقديم الأغنيات الجماهيرية، بل أصبح واحدًا من المطربين الذين يبحثون عن تجديد صورتهم الفنية باستمرار". ### خاص.. موعد بدء تصوير مسلسل أحمد السقا الجديد "كتف في كتف" ينافس الفنان أحمد السقا في الموسم الرمضاني المقبل 2027 بمسلسل جديد يحمل اسم “كتف في كتف”، بمشاركة نخبة من نجوم الفن، على رأسهم أحمد غزي، ومن إخراج شادي عبد السلام، وإنتاج صادق الصباح. وعلم “وشوشة” من مصادره الخاصة تفاصيل جديدة عن مسلسل “كتف في كتف”، حيث أكدت المصادر أن العمل يتكون من 15 حلقة فقط، وتدور أحداثه في إطار اجتماعي بعيدًا عن الكوميديا. وأضافت المصادر أن أحمد السقا وفريق عمل المسلسل سيبدأون تصوير مشاهده خلال الأسبوع المقبل، استعدادًا للحاق بالموسم الرمضاني المقبل.
